A deliberative scoring or ranked-choice vote is preferable to a simple majority because all three options have meaningful trade-offs.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"Agent A","position":"Favors spending the full budget on an inter-city tournament with prizes and a buffet to maximize the club's visibility.","influence":0.33},{"agent":"Agent B","position":"Favors spending the full budget on educational materials and new chessboards to strengthen the club's long-term instructional capacity.","influence":0.4},{"agent":"Agent C","position":"Favors dividing the budget equally between a smaller tournament and new equipment as a balanced alternative.","influence":0.27}],"recommended_resolution":"collaborative","governance_reasoning":"The three positions reflect competing but legitimate goals, and none has an overwhelming evidentiary advantage. Use collaborative deliberation to establish weighted criteria, require each option to address cost-effectiveness and measurable outcomes, then apply a ranked or scored social-choice vote. A data-informed hybrid allocation may emerge, but it should not be imposed as an arbitrary 50/50 compromise."}
